human_review_checklist.item: No section headings in cover letter
human_review_checklist.note: Proper prose format throughout, no ## or other headers

human_review_checklist.item: Cover letter has authentic opening hook
human_review_checklist.note: Opens with engaging question about what keeps candidate up at night - compelling entry

human_review_checklist.item: Company name and role appear naturally
human_review_checklist.note: Lindy AI mentioned in salutation; role referenced naturally once
Multi-agent systems and forward-deployed experience not explicitly acknowledged
Some phrases like 'technical depth and user impact' feel slightly generic
Email and phone in both documents
Most bullets include numbers: ~100 users, 300+, tens of thousands, 3 junior engineers
Clean, consistent formatting throughout both documents

strengths: Specific, verifiable claims throughout (exact numbers for users, documents, team size)
Strong keyword coverage for AI/LLM role: Python, LangChain, Agents SDK, MCP, pgvector, RAG, rerankers
Engaging opening hook in cover letter - 'what keeps me up at night' draws reader in
Measurable outcomes in resume bullets: ~100 users piloted, 300+ onboarding, tens of thousands of documents
Proper prose format in cover letter - no section headers or broken formatting
Clear narrative voice with personal perspective ('I've spent three years', 'the overlap was hard to miss')
Contacts present in both resume and cover letter
revision_suggestions: Add a line showing research into Lindy AI - reference their specific product, approach, or recent announcement
Explicitly connect modular component architecture to multi-agent system design
Consider adding forward-deployed or customer-facing implementation language if applicable
The cover letter would be stronger with one specific insight about Lindy's approach
weaknesses: Limited company-specificity: only generic references to 'autonomous AI agents for professionals' - could apply to many companies
Multi-agent systems experience not explicitly demonstrated despite role requiring it
Forward deployed / customer-facing deployment experience unclear (appears consulting-focused)
Some template-adjacent language: 'where technical depth and user impact both matter' could appear elsewhere
